title: Logarithmic differential coefficient restriction preserves test sequences
statement:
Let $N\hookrightarrow Z$ be a closed immersion of smooth finite-type $\mathbf Q$-schemes, let $B$ be a finite ordered simple normal crossings boundary on $Z$ transverse to $N$, and let $K\subset\mathcal O_N$ be coherent, with positive integer mark $d$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-weil-closed-immersion] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] [pqf-def-coherent]. For an ideal $T$ set $\operatorname{ord}_x(T)=\sup\{q\in\mathbf Z_{\ge0}:T_x\subseteq\mathfrak m_x^q\}$, with $\operatorname{ord}_x(0)=\infty$. Put $\operatorname{cosupp}(K,d)=\{x:K_x\subseteq\mathfrak m_x^d\}$. Assume $\operatorname{ord}_xK\le d$ near this cosupport. Define $D_B^jK$ to be the ideal generated by $K$ and its iterated derivatives of length at most $j$ by $\mathbf Q$-derivations preserving every boundary ideal on $N$. Suppose a section $h\in D_B^{d-1}K$ cuts out a smooth hypersurface $H\subset N$ transverse to $B$, and has order one everywhere under consideration. Set $L=d!$ and construct the coherent ideal
$$C=\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}\bigl((D_B^jK)\mathcal O_H\bigr)^{L/(d-j)}\subset\mathcal O_H.$$
Then the marked data $(Z,N,B,K,d)$ and $(Z,H,B,C,L)$ have identical cosupports as subsets of $Z$ and identical finite test sequences. Here a test sequence allows open restrictions, products with a line, blowups with smooth center in cosupport having normal crossings with the boundary, and blowups of intersections of two boundary components. For a cosupport blowup take strict transform of the smooth support and divide the total ideal transform by the mark-th exceptional power; for the other two operations use ordinary pullback [def-nagata-global-blowup] [def-nagata-strict-transform]. A line product adjoins its zero section to the boundary. The assertion identifies the permissible centers and the subsequent cosupports at every stage, not just at stage zero. Different choices of $h$, etale coordinates or representatives having the same test sequences give coefficient presentations having the same test sequences in the common ambient scheme. These identifications commute with smooth pullback and restriction. If $C=0$ on an open component of $H$, its cosupport is that entire smooth component, and blowing up that component removes this coefficient presentation's cosupport there. No claim that a nonzero coefficient ideal always results is made.

proof.text:
All local rings of $N$ and $H$ are regular by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular]. Choose minimal generators of their maximal ideals. They are regular sequences by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], and [lem-pur-regular-sequence-graded-polynomial] identifies the associated graded ring with a polynomial ring over the residue field. It is a domain. Consequently, for any stalk ideal $I$ and integers $q,r\ge1$,
$$I^r\subseteq\mathfrak m^{rq}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad I\subseteq\mathfrak m^q.$$
Indeed the reverse implication is multiplication; if $f\in I\setminus\mathfrak m^q$ has order $s<q$, the nonzero initial form of $f$ has nonzero $r$th power in degree $rs<rq$. Thus a weighted sum $\sum I_j^{L/b_j}$ has order at least $L$ exactly when every $I_j$ has order at least $b_j$. This also covers zero ideals and unit ideals. We will use this argument on every smooth transformed support.

source.place: Agent proof of the coefficient restriction argument; ILO VIII 2.3.13 and BM 2008 §§3--4 (WANTED locally)

proof.text: Put $J_j=D_B^jK$ and $b_j=d-j$. A derivation maps $\mathfrak m^q$ into $\mathfrak m^{q-1}$ by the product rule. Hence $x\in\operatorname{cosupp}(K,d)$ implies $\operatorname{ord}_xJ_j\ge b_j$. Since $h\in J_{d-1}$, this cosupport lies in $H$. The same order inequalities hold after restriction to $H$, so step 1 gives $\operatorname{cosupp}(K,d)\subseteq\operatorname{cosupp}(C,L)$. Notice that the hypothesis is a chosen transverse order-one section; we do not infer its existence merely from maximal order.

source.place: Agent proof of the coefficient restriction argument; ILO VIII 2.3.13 and BM 2008 §§3--4 (WANTED locally)

proof.text:
Work locally along $H$. Transversality means that $h$ together with the boundary equations has independent differentials; extend these to a basis of the differential fibre. [lem-pur-etale-at-point-from-differentials] gives an etale chart $(w,h)$ with the boundary among the $w$ coordinates. The coordinate/Taylor assertion of [lem-trf-implicit-taylor-coordinate-calculus] gives regular normal coefficients
$$a_{\alpha i}=\frac{1}{i!}(\partial_h^i f_\alpha)|_H$$
for a finite set of local generators $f_\alpha$ of $K$. Their expansions along $H$ are $f_\alpha=\sum_{i\ge0}a_{\alpha i}h^i$. More precisely this identity is in the formal neighbourhood of $H$, using its coordinate retraction: it follows by successively lifting the etale chart across $(h)^n/(h)^{n+1}$ with [lem-weil-pbc-flat-unramified-formally-etale], since etale means flat and unramified [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Each lift is unique, so these lifts are compatible. This is a normal formal expansion, not an assertion that an etale chart is an algebraic product.

source.place: Agent proof of the coefficient restriction argument; ILO VIII 2.3.13 and BM 2008 §§3--4 (WANTED locally)

proof.text: Let $A_i=(a_{\alpha i})_{\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal O_H$ for $0\le i<d$, and put $A=\sum_{i<d}A_i^{L/(d-i)}$. Since $\partial_h$ preserves the boundary ideals, $A_i\subseteq J_i\mathcal O_H$, and therefore $A\subseteq C$. At any $x\in H$, in the normal expansion of step 3 the ideal of the point is $(\mathfrak m_{H,x},h)$. A series lies in its $d$th power precisely when its coefficient of $h^i$ lies in $\mathfrak m_{H,x}^{d-i}$ for all $i<d$: compare monomials, and group all terms $i\ge d$ into $(h)^d$. This calculation detects actual stalk membership: on each quotient by $(h)^d$ the etale formal lifting identifies the quotient with $\mathcal O_H[h]/(h^d)$ locally, and $(h^d)\subseteq\mathfrak m_x^d$. It works at nonclosed points as well. Thus step 1 and the finite generators show $\operatorname{cosupp}(K,d)=\operatorname{cosupp}(A,L)$ as subsets of $H$. Together with steps 2 and $A\subseteq C$ this proves the asserted equality at stage zero.

source.place: Agent proof of the coefficient restriction argument; ILO VIII 2.3.13 and BM 2008 §§3--4 (WANTED locally)

proof.text:
We prove equality at every finite stage by induction on the length of a common test prefix. The induction data consist of the transforms $K_t$, $J_{j,t}$ (with their own marks $d$ and $d-j$), $C_t$, $A_{i,t}$, $A_t$, and the strict-transform hypersurface $H_t$ with local equation $h_t$ transformed with mark $1$. For any prefix allowed for $K$, [lem-trf-logarithmic-derivative-single-transform] gives, inductively,
$$J_{j,t}\subseteq D_{B_t}^jK_t.$$
To justify the iteration, transform the preceding inclusion with the same mark $d-j$; pullback and division by the same exceptional power preserve inclusion, and then apply the single-step inclusion to $K_t$. Also $(h_t)\subseteq J_{d-1,t}$, by transforming the initial inclusion $(h)\subseteq J_{d-1}$. Derivatives lower order, so $\operatorname{cosupp}(K_t,d)\subseteq V(h_t)$. Thus the hypersurface continues to contain the original cosupport, including in charts where it disappears.

source.place: Agent proof of the coefficient restriction argument; ILO VIII 2.3.13 and BM 2008 §§3--4 (WANTED locally)

proof.text: Let $T$ be a permissible cosupport center. Step 5 puts every point of $T$ in $V(h_t)$. Apply [lem-trf-marked-controlled-blowup-charts] first to $((h_t),1)$ on $N_t$: its ideal-power assertion gives $(h_t)\subseteq\mathcal I_{T,N_t}$. Thus $T\subset H_t$ scheme-theoretically. Apply the node to $N_t\hookrightarrow Z_t$ with $(K_t,d)$, and to $H_t\hookrightarrow Z_t$ with the zero ideal and mark $1$ (whose order condition is automatic). Its explicit support identifications give $N_{t+1}\cong\operatorname{Bl}_T N_t$ and $H_{t+1}\cong\operatorname{Bl}_T H_t$ inside the same ambient blowup. The chart formulas make these strict transforms smooth, preserve the boundary condition, and make controlled ideal transforms regular. Locally the center ideal on $N_t$ has the form $(h_t,u_1,\ldots,u_r)$. In a chart meeting the strict transform of $H_t$ the exceptional coordinate can be chosen $e=u_k$ and $h_t=e h_{t+1}$. In the $h_t$-chart the transformed section is $1$, so step 5 makes the cosupport of $K_{t+1}$ empty there. If a component of $H_t$ is the center, its strict transform is empty by the same cited node; this includes zero-dimensional components.

source.place: Agent proof of the coefficient restriction argument; ILO VIII 2.3.13 and BM 2008 §§3--4 (WANTED locally)

proof.text:
In the charts of step 6, write a transformed generator in the normal formal expansion $f_{\alpha,t}=\sum_i a_{\alpha i,t}h_t^i$. The center-power conclusion of [lem-trf-marked-controlled-blowup-charts] gives $f_{\alpha,t}\in(h_t,u)^d$ when the center is permissible. Comparing powers of $h_t$ gives $a_{\alpha i,t}\in(u)^{d-i}$ for $i<d$. Direct substitution gives
$$e^{-d}\sigma^*f_{\alpha,t}=\sum_{i\ge0}e^{i-d}\sigma_H^*a_{\alpha i,t}\,h_{t+1}^i.$$
For $i<d$ these are exactly the controlled transforms of the coefficient ideals with mark $d-i$; for $i\ge d$ the powers of $e$ are nonnegative. All coefficients are regular. The coordinate retraction extends to these formal charts by fixing the coefficients on $H_{t+1}$; any later smooth center in $H_{t+1}$ has ideal $(h_{t+1},\mathcal I_{T,H_{t+1}})$ in this formal neighbourhood. Thus the same substitution applies again, without choosing a different Taylor expansion. The finite-quotient lifting and order test of steps 3--4 justify computing this way in stalks.

source.place: Agent proof of the coefficient restriction argument; ILO VIII 2.3.13 and BM 2008 §§3--4 (WANTED locally)

proof.text: An exceptional boundary-intersection center is transverse to $H_t$: in boundary-adapted coordinates it is $(x_1,x_2)$, with $h_t$ an independent coordinate. The regular coordinate blowup charts of [lem-trf-permissible-coordinate-chart] are $x_1=e$, $x_2=e v$ and the symmetric chart. Thus $h_{t+1}=h_t$, the supports are inverse images (also their strict transforms), and substitution in the normal expansion gives $a_{\alpha i,t+1}=\sigma_H^*a_{\alpha i,t}$. This operation uses total pullback and introduces no factor $e^{-d}$. These charts are regular and of finite type over $\mathbf Q$, so [lem-trf-regular-perfect-field-smooth] makes the supports smooth; $\mathbf Q$ is perfect since a nonconstant irreducible polynomial in characteristic zero has nonzero derivative and is coprime to it. The displayed boundary parameters have normal crossings and are independent of the support equations. Products with a line and open restrictions leave the same normal expansion, with the coefficients pulled back. The new line coordinate is independent of $h_t$, so adjoining its zero divisor does not change this argument.

source.place: Agent proof of the coefficient restriction argument; ILO VIII 2.3.13 and BM 2008 §§3--4 (WANTED locally)

proof.text:
For every shared operation, restriction of the tracked ideals to the strict transform of $H_t$ commutes with their transforms: in a chart meeting that transform both operations are pullback followed by division by the same exceptional power, and the other cases use ordinary pullback. Therefore
$$C_t=\sum_{j<d}(J_{j,t}\mathcal O_{H_t})^{L/(d-j)},\qquad A_t=\sum_{i<d}A_{i,t}^{L/(d-i)},\qquad A_t\subseteq C_t.$$
For example, under a cosupport blowup, $(e^{-(d-j)}J_{j,t})^{L/(d-j)}=e^{-L}J_{j,t}^{L/(d-j)}$, so the weighted sums really do transform with mark $L$. The regularity and identifications of the strict transforms used here are supplied by [lem-trf-marked-controlled-blowup-charts].

source.place: Agent proof of the coefficient restriction argument; ILO VIII 2.3.13 and BM 2008 §§3--4 (WANTED locally)

proof.text: At the end of a common prefix, step 5 confines the cosupport of $K_t$ to $H_t$, and steps 7--8 identify the $A_{i,t}$ as its normal coefficient ideals. The coefficient order test of step 4 and the power test of step 1 give $\operatorname{cosupp}(K_t,d)=\operatorname{cosupp}(A_t,L)$. Step 5 also gives $\operatorname{ord}_xJ_{j,t}\ge d-j$ on that cosupport, so restriction and step 9 give its inclusion in $\operatorname{cosupp}(C_t,L)$. Conversely $A_t\subseteq C_t$ gives $\operatorname{cosupp}(C_t,L)\subseteq\operatorname{cosupp}(A_t,L)$. All three cosupports therefore agree. Consequently a smooth center is permissible for either datum exactly when it is permissible for both, since the ambient boundary is identical. The other test operations are already common. This closes the induction, with base case step 4, and proves equality for every finite word, in both directions.

source.place: Agent proof of the coefficient restriction argument; ILO VIII 2.3.13 and BM 2008 §§3--4 (WANTED locally)

proof.text: Changing $h$ repeats the argument with the same original marked datum, so the two coefficient presentations have the same test sequences by transitivity of equality of sets of words. The same argument applies to any representative already assumed to have the same test sequences. Coordinates merely computed the intrinsically defined ideals $D_B^jK$ and their restrictions. Thus these comparisons require neither a preferred hypersurface nor an equality between two newly chosen coefficient ideals.

source.place: Agent proof of the coefficient restriction argument; ILO VIII 2.3.13 and BM 2008 §§3--4 (WANTED locally)

proof.text: The smooth pullback equality of [lem-trf-logarithmic-derivative-single-transform] identifies the pulled-back $C$ with the coefficient ideal of the pulled-back datum; restriction and the finite sums and powers commute with pullback. Orders and cosupports also pull back: apply [lem-trf-smooth-local-tangent-cone-extension] to the induced essentially smooth local map. Its identification of the base graded algebra with the constant-polynomial part is injective, since residue-field extension is faithful; hence a nonzero initial form keeps its degree. Coherence supplies finite ideal generators, so the same assertion holds for ideal order. The local maps are essentially smooth by the affine smooth dictionary [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine], followed by localization. Finally [lem-trf-marked-controlled-blowup-charts] explicitly identifies the strict supports with $\operatorname{Bl}_T N_t$ and $\operatorname{Bl}_T H_t$ compatibly with smooth base change; its controlled-transform formulas commute with that base change as well. For exceptional blowups the two charts in step 8 pull back to the identical two formulas. This proves compatibility of all the identifications with smooth pullback, and open restriction is its special case.

source.place: Agent proof of the coefficient restriction argument; ILO VIII 2.3.13 and BM 2008 §§3--4 (WANTED locally)

proof.text: If $C=0$ on an open component of $H$, the definition gives every point of that component order at least $L$. Blowing up that smooth component is permissible, and [lem-trf-marked-controlled-blowup-charts] says its strict transform disappears. Hence the coefficient cosupport there disappears. Equality of cosupports after this word, already proved, gives the same conclusion for the original datum. In particular no argument above needs $C$ to be nonzero.
